items.title: Jean Bach interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, October 18, 1995
items.q: Bob Bach, my late husband, was doing a special on Ellington for PBS. And he got what they call sort of “witness spots” you know for people that had known him, and told little highlights about their lives. And of course I had nine million adventures, I couldn’t wait to get on.

ctx.x: They were kind of night owls.

That’s it. So Ellington finally came in, in a stunning silk robe, and very courtly, “how lovely to see you.” I said, “well you did say to come by.” I looked like, well I can’t say co-ed, ‘cause we only had girls and boys schools then, but you know I had the little bowler hat and the polo coat and the little white gloves and everything. And so years later, Bob Bach, my late husband, was doing a special on Ellington for PBS. And he got what they call sort of “witness spots” you know for people that had known him,…
He was never at a loss, was he?
